newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-CHANG IN SPOTLIGHT AS AUSTRALIAN OPEN KICKS OFF.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-CHANG IN SPOTLIGHT AS AUSTRALIAN OPEN KICKS OFF.

text.p: Play began at the Australian Open tennis tournament on Monday with world number two Michael Chang, aiming for the second grand slam title of his career, kicking off the action against Belgian qualifier Kris Goossens.
Chang, who has been in superb form leading up to the first grand slam of the year, is seeded second for the tournament behind fellow-American Pete Sampras.
German women's number one Steffi Graf, the hot favourite at Melbourne Park, was to open the centre court action against Janette Husarova of Slovakia at 10.45 a.m. (2345 GMT Sunday).
Graf, the four-times champion, is making her first appearance in Melbourne for three years after missing the last two Opens through injury.
Chang, 24, has only won one grand slam title, the French Open eight years ago, but came close to a second in Melbourne last year when he fell to Boris Becker in the final.
The right-hander beat his main rival for the Open title at the weekend, downing Pete Sampras in the final of the Colonial Classic exhibition warm-up event.
Germany's Michael Stich, seeded 15, follows Graf on centre court when he meets Sweden's Patrik Fredriksson.
Defending champion Boris Becker, the sixth seed, meets Carlos Moya in the final match of the day session on centre court.
